identity.name: Dynamical MFV inverse-seesaw Majoraxion dark matter (CASE A)

Unbroken Z2 parity forbids Higgs-dark-doublet mixing and makes the lightest eta_R/eta_I state a scalar dark matter candidate.
The analysis assumes scalar dark matter with lambda_5 < 0, so eta_R is the dark matter candidate.
micrOMEGAS is used to compute thermal relic abundance, with Planck-compatible regions identified in eta_R mass.

unresolved_items: The exact XENON1T likelihood or exclusion curve was not rerun.
Mass-splitting thresholds for inelastic Z exchange were not digitized.
Vacuum-stability details are retained as a theory filter rather than a recast likelihood.

particle_content.note: The paper entertains an intermediate-mass pseudo-Goldstone boson G_I with mass between dark-energy and dark-matter PGB scales that contributes a fraction f_I of the matter density.

symmetries.note: The underlying picture uses spontaneous breaking of an approximate U(1)^n flavor symmetry near the Planck scale, with small explicit breaking terms producing the PGB potential.

interactions.note: The model is represented by cosine PGB potential terms and affects clustering through the effective pressure/sound speed of the scalar field.

production_mechanism.note: The field is frozen while H > m_I and behaves as dark matter after it starts oscillating when H is comparable to m_I.

cosmological_history.note: The paper tracks the field as a cosmological-constant-like component before oscillation and as dark matter afterward, with CMB effects if the component is non-negligible at decoupling.

parameter_ranges.note: The paper gives F_I/M_Pl from 0.01 to 1, Lambda_I from 3e-3 to 30 eV, m_I from 1e-33 to 1e-23 eV, and f_I from 1e-3 to 1 as indicative ranges.
